headline.topic: Results are now verified against the league, not just internally
headline.finding: 32 of 32 teams reconcile exactly on W/L/T/PF/PA against NFL.com once the official scores for the checked weeks are added.

headline.topic: The committed data is a week-and-a-half stale
headline.finding: 17 games that had already finished were absent from the committed snapshot. They are listed, not back-filled.
The only opening-line source in the repository covers one season, one sportsbook, and has no moneyline at all.
P(home win) is printed to 4 decimals from Phi(spread / sigma). Recomputing it from the published side reproduces every one of the 15 games within 0.0014.

headline.topic: Fair, market and difference are now three columns
headline.finding: Across the board the fair side and the market side correlate at 0.823 (n=15); the average hold is 0.0422.
2 of 9 strategies have a positive ROI that their own test does not support, and 0 reward is paid.

headline.topic: Depth is measurable, but not from an official source
headline.finding: The official roster and injury pages carry no depth ordinal; every 1st/2nd/3rd-string value is third-party and labelled.

headline.topic: Official correlations are mostly uncomputable yet
headline.finding: The official season-leader pages give team-level correlations at n=32 and a year-over-year point-differential persistence of 0.5031 (n=32), but not the per-game QB-to-receiver pair the parlay pricing needs.
Eight rules, four evaluable today, with an explicit asymmetry: promotion is slow, demotion is fast.
